question_snapshot.stem_en: In Bela Banerjee, a permanent acquisition law capped compensation at the land’s market value on 31 December 1946, regardless of when it was later acquired. Why was that cap invalid under the then Article 31(2)?
options_en: Every earlier valuation date was necessarily unconstitutional.
The arbitrary ceiling could deny the owner the just equivalent of the property taken.
The legislature had no power to prescribe any compensation principles.
Compensation depended solely on the acquiring authority’s discretion.

question_snapshot.stem_en: In R.C. Cooper (1970), payment of acquisition compensation through bonds was assessed by reference to which consideration?
options_en: A bond’s face value alone, regardless of its present value
Compensation could be paid only as immediate cash
The money value at expropriation, including the effect of interest terms
The acquiring authority’s description of the payment as compensation

question_snapshot.stem_en: A law declares that it implements Article 39(b). Its defenders argue that this declaration alone prevents a court from examining whether it actually serves that policy. Which response is correct?
options_en: The declaration is conclusive once the law states Article 39(b) in its preamble.
Only the law’s title may be examined; its actual policy connection cannot be reviewed.
The declaration alone does not exclude judicial examination of the policy connection.
The connection may be reviewed only if the President withholds assent.

question_snapshot.stem_en: A State Legislature enacts two laws: one concerns a category specified in Article 31A(1), and the other genuinely implements Article 39(b) for purposes of Article 31C. Both receive only the Governor’s assent and neither is reserved for the President’s consideration. The State claims their respective special protections against Article 14 challenges. Which assessment is correct?
options_en: Both special protections apply solely because the laws address the specified subjects.
Both laws are necessarily invalid because the special protections are unavailable.
Both special protections require reservation for Presidential consideration and Presidential assent; their absence does not alone decide either law’s validity.
Article 31A requires Presidential assent, but Article 31C never imposes that condition on a State law.

Officials take a person’s land for a public project but acknowledge that no law authorises the deprivation. Which response correctly applies Article 300A?
options_en: A public purpose alone replaces the need for authority of law.
Removal of property from Part III removes every constitutional protection against deprivation.
Any executive announcement is sufficient without legal authority.
Deprivation must have authority of law; public purpose alone does not meet that requirement.

Consider Article 32:
1. The right to move the Supreme Court to enforce Part III rights is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. Article 32 is a general direct remedy for every statutory dispute even when no Fundamental Right is implicated.
Which is/are correct?

Consider Article 32:
1. The right to move the Supreme Court to enforce Part III rights is itself a Fundamental Right.
2. Article 32 is a general direct remedy for every statutory dispute even when no Fundamental Right is implicated.
Which is/are correct?
Which Article did Dr. B. R. Ambedkar describe as the Constitution’s heart and soul because it supplies an effective remedy for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
Which statement correctly distinguishes Article 32(1) from Article 32(4)?
options_en: Clause (1) guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court to enforce Part III rights; clause (4) bars suspension of that right except as otherwise provided by the Constitution.
Clause (1) concerns every statutory dispute; clause (4) permits suspension by any executive circular.
Clause (1) concerns High Courts alone; clause (4) lists the five writs.
Clause (4) prohibits suspension without any constitutional exception.

question_snapshot.stem_en: Which statement correctly distinguishes Article 32(1) from Article 32(4)?
options_en: Clause (1) guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court to enforce Part III rights; clause (4) bars suspension of that right except as otherwise provided by the Constitution.
Clause (1) concerns every statutory dispute; clause (4) permits suspension by any executive circular.
Clause (1) concerns High Courts alone; clause (4) lists the five writs.
Clause (4) prohibits suspension without any constitutional exception.

Which set contains the five writs specifically named in Article 32(2)?
Under Article 32(3), which authority may by law empower another court to exercise the relevant writ powers within its local jurisdiction, without prejudice to the Supreme Court’s powers?
options_en: The Supreme Court solely through its procedural rules
A High Court solely through a full-court administrative resolution

question_snapshot.stem_en: A claimant seeks enforcement of a statutory legal right and identifies no Fundamental Right violation. Which statement correctly describes the constitutional scope of writ powers?
options_en: Article 32 automatically covers every such claim.
Article 226 is limited to Fundamental Rights alone.
No constitutional writ power can ever address a statutory right.
Article 226 can extend to other legal rights, subject to applicable legal rules.

question_snapshot.stem_en: A respondent authority is seated outside a High Court’s territory, but a material part of the cause of action arises within it. Is the authority’s outside location alone sufficient to deny jurisdiction under Article 226(2)?
options_en: Yes; territorial jurisdiction depends exclusively on the respondent authority’s seat.
No; a material cause-of-action connection can support jurisdiction despite that location.
Yes; Article 226(2) applies only when the whole cause of action arises within the territory.
No; the claimant’s residence alone is sufficient even without any material cause-of-action connection.

During a National Emergency, a valid Article 359(1) order suspends the right to move any court to enforce Article 14 in the relevant area and period. A petition seeks only that enforcement. Can filing it under Article 226 instead of Article 32, by itself, avoid the suspension?
options_en: Yes; Article 359 concerns the Supreme Court alone.
Yes; every Article 226 petition is immune from Article 359.
No; “any court” includes the High Court for the enforcement specified in the order.
No; a National Emergency permanently repeals Article 226.

question_snapshot.stem_en:
Assertion (A): Article 32 jurisdiction is an integral part of the Constitution’s basic structure.
Reason (R): Fundamental Rights require an effective remedy for their enforcement when violated.
In light of Fertilizer Corporation Kamgar Union, choose the correct answer.
options_en: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A.
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
